title: Smallest Missing Non-negative Integer After Operations
summary: Given an integer array nums and a value, you can add or subtract the value from any element in nums.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a value, you can add or subtract the value from any element in nums. The task is to find the largest non-negative integer that is not present in the array after performing any number of such operations. The MEX of an array is the smallest non-negative integer not present in the array.
constraints: You may add or subtract value from any array element any number of times.
The MEX is the smallest non-negative integer missing after those operations.
Return the largest MEX that can be achieved.
reference_solution:
def maximum_mex_after_steps(nums,value):
    counts=[0]*value
    for number in nums:counts[number%value]+=1
    answer=0
    while counts[answer%value]:
        counts[answer%value]-=1;answer+=1
    return answer
hints: Adding or subtracting value never changes an integer's remainder modulo value.
Count how many input values belong to each remainder class.
Try to construct zero, one, two, and so on, consuming one matching remainder each time.
The first candidate whose remainder count is exhausted is exactly the maximum achievable MEX.
editorial: The first candidate whose remainder count is exhausted is exactly the maximum achievable MEX.

tests.explanation: Residues can represent zero through three, so the best MEX is four.
Only zero and one can both be represented before residue two is unavailable.
